evidence.title: PAIX Data Centres announces the construction of a new ultra-modern data centre in Dakar, Senegal
evidence.excerpt: PAIX announced DKR-1 after purchasing its Dakar land and reported a planned first phase with 1.2 MW of IT load and colocation service.

metadata.reported_land_status: PAIX Data Centres purchased the land to build the buildings that would house the data-centre equipment.
metadata.status_scope: The land-purchase statement supports one historical site_control observation as of January 27, 2025. The headline's generic construction wording, future-tense project description, expected construction jobs, and forecast 2026 operation do not establish groundbreaking, mobilization, clearing, site preparation, civil works, excavation, foundations, shell, MEP, energization, commissioning, completion, occupancy, operation, or current load.
metadata.status_freshness_guardrail: The source is not a dated current-status update after January 27, 2025. It cannot prove that site control remained unchanged or that physical construction or operation had begun by the 2026 retrieval date.
metadata.forecast_guardrail: The source supplies only a calendar-year forecast with no exact target date. It creates no target_date, commissioning, completion, energization, operational, occupancy, service-availability, utilization, or current-load observation.
metadata.capacity_scope: The 1.2 MW is retained as planned critical-IT design capacity. A nearby paragraph qualifies the facility goal as up to 1.2 MW; it is not gross facility demand, grid connection, generation, contracted supply, current load, measured consumption, or annual energy.
metadata.specification_discrepancy_guardrail: The same disclosure reports approximately 918 square metres in prose and 900 square metres in a feature list. Neither value is normalized into capacity, geometry, or building area, and neither is used to reconcile the standing page's later 300-cabinet figure.
metadata.operating_model_scope: The source explicitly describes future colocation services. This supports a planned-project colocation classification only; it does not establish current service availability, occupancy, a tenant, a customer, or operation.
metadata.role_scope: PAIX purchased the land, announced the development, and describes the data centre as its project. This supports PAIX Data Centres as developer only; no owner, operator, landlord, tenant, user, customer, utility, contractor, or power-supplier role is inferred.
metadata.workload_guardrail: Cloud, content, social-media, connectivity, CDN, and digital-services language describes expected customers or market context. It creates no normalized workload, installed hardware, rack density, tenant, customer, user, model, or present compute observation.
metadata.energy_guardrail: The planned critical-IT design value is not converted into annual energy because there is no dated operating state, utilization, operating-hour, current-draw, gross-load, or measured-consumption observation. The 2030 corporate renewable-energy commitment creates no site energy source, renewable fraction, generation, PUE, WUE, emissions, or current-power claim.
metadata.entity_model_guardrail: The campus entity is an internal parent container for the single DKR-1 development project at one address. It is not a second data centre, building, phase, project, construction start, or physical-site count and must not be added to its child.
metadata.collision_guardrail: DKR-1 is not merged with PAIX facilities in Accra, Nairobi, Djibouti, Côte d'Ivoire, Rwanda, or with another operator's Dakar facility.
metadata.imagery_guardrail: Publisher images, maps, satellite imagery, aerial imagery, computer vision, and analyst geolocation contribute nothing to lifecycle, capacity, operating status, type, workload, energy, PUE, or physical-site count.
